title: Precise Graphic Placement | Clo 2026.0 Features Deep Dive
description:

Check out other new features here: https://clo3d.com/en/clo/features

markdown_content: ## Edit Graphic Tool: Open Graphics and Start Custom Measurements This section explains how to access the **Edit Graphic** tool, switch to the correct graphic, and begin the **Custom Measurements** workflow from the right-click menu. 1. Open the **Edit Graphic** tool (shown as the tool panel on the screen). 2. Select the graphic you want to adjust (example: the **front chest** graphic). 3. In the **object browser**, confirm you’ve switched to the corresponding **graphic tab**. 4. Right-click directly on the selected graphic. 5. Choose **Custom Measurements** from the right-click menu. After selecting **Custom Measurements**, the property editor appears and a purple interaction indicator appears near the cursor. You can then click on specific parts of the jersey **pattern** (e.g., edges or points) to generate measurement references. > Key behavior: the measurement tool requires intersections with the graphic/pattern context. Some points won’t work unless they intersect correctly (e.g., a corner point may fail, while a **high point shoulder** point will work). ## Selecting Intersecting Pattern Points and Creating a Measurement This section covers how to pick valid pattern sections/edges that intersect with the graphic, and how the tool creates a numeric custom measurement once you click. - Click on an eligible point/edge of the pattern while the cursor shows the custom measurement interaction. - The measurement value is generated after the click (example shown: **9.581**). Workflow notes: - Use the left mouse button to select the measurement anchor(s), and then continue through the tool’s prompts. - The created measurement appears in the UI (example: **Graphical Outlines** context is referenced in the created measurement panel). Once created, the **property editor** shows the selected custom measurement and options to manage it. ## Measurement Properties: Rename and Control Placement Updates This section describes the measurement property editor features, including renaming and how placement behavior is tied to outlines. In the property editor: - The custom measurement can be **renamed**. - The measurement shows what it is **locked to** (example shown: **Update locked to Graphic Outline**). - There is a **Placement Update** option that affects how the measurement updates when the graphic moves. Example behavior demonstrated: - The measurement can update in response to graphic movement depending on the selected lock/update mode. - A created measurement is shown as being linked to a specific outline reference (initially **Graphic Outline**). ## Locking Behavior: Graphic Outline vs Pattern Outline This section explains how changing the lock target changes where the measurement stays anchored when you move the graphic. ### 1) Locked to **Graphic Outline** - When the measurement is locked to **Graphic Outline**, moving the graphic causes the **measurement placement to move with the graphic**. - It does **not** remain fixed to the original shoulder point; instead, it updates based on where the graphic’s outline is placed. Reset behavior (as demonstrated): - Use **Control Z** to undo/reset after experimenting with lock behavior. ### 2) Locked to **Pattern Outline** - Change the lock target from **Graphic Outline** to **Pattern Outline**. - Now, when you move the graphic, the measurement remains anchored to the **pattern outline** reference. - If you move the graphic so it no longer intersects the relevant area, the measurement reference disappears, but you can keep moving until it intersects again. This makes **Pattern Outline** useful when you want measurements to stay tied to the garment pattern rather than the graphic’s outline. ## Placement Editing: Adjusting the Numeric Value This section shows how to directly edit the measurement’s placement value. - In the placement controls, you can change the numeric value (example shown: changing from approximately **9.8** to **9.5**). - After updating, the measurement reflects the new value (example shown: the placement updates to **9.5**). ## Custom Measurements vs POM (Points of Measure) This section clarifies how **Custom Measurements** relates to the **POM** tab, and where to use each. - **POM** (Points of Measure) exists under the **POM tab**. - **Custom Measurements** is a different system used inside the **Edit Graphic** tool: - Select the graphic in **Edit Graphic** - Right-click → **Custom Measurements** The custom measurement tool provides instructions based on what outline mode you select. ## Custom Measurement Tool Modes and Cursor Instructions This section captures the on-cursor instructions and the different behaviors for **pattern outline** and **free custom measurements**. When using the **custom measurement tool**, the cursor/instructions indicate: - **For pattern outline:** click **pattern outline** for a **straight measurement**. - **For free custom measurements:** **hold Shift** to snap to **corners** or **point recommendations**. The tool also shows available anchor options with visual indicators: - Purple highlights indicate selectable “middle” parts/candidate points. - Red points indicate **suggestion points**. ## Shift-Snap and Suggested Points (Corners, Middles, and Recommendations) This section explains how to use **Shift** snapping and the purple/red point suggestions to place measurements precisely. Demonstrated steps: 1. Hold **Shift** to enable snapping. 2. Zoom in to see additional snap targets: - **Purple** “middle” segments/points (multiple middle areas are shown). - **Red** suggestion points. 3. You can: - Click using the suggested points (red points), or - Click in the center area directly (within the selectable region). Example placement described: - Choose a start such as **high point shoulder** and end at the **center**. - The tool outputs a measurement pair (example shown: **12** and **4.1**), and the graphic is placed accordingly. ## Using Placement Controls After Creating a Custom Measurement This section covers how to move the graphic using the created custom measurement’s placement controls. After placing a custom measurement: - Use the **placement** controls to move the graphic while maintaining the intended measurement relationship. - Placement is described as “all set” after the measurement is created and anchored. ## Quick Interaction Controls: Turn Custom Measurement On/Off with Shift This section documents the ability to toggle snap/points and measurement interaction using **Shift**. Demonstrated behavior: - Right-click → **Custom Measurement** - **Shift** toggles the snap/selection points: - “Shift to turn it on” - “Shift to turn it off” - You can repeat toggling as needed, then continue selecting the desired anchor/bounding box area. If you don’t want the suggestion snapping: - Select the **bounding box** and click the area you want. - Then decide what the measurement should be **locked to**. ## Managing Multiple Custom Measurements and Renaming This section explains how custom measurements accumulate in the UI and how to create additional ones for different placement needs. - All custom measurements appear in a list/panel on the side. - Each measurement can be **named**. - You can create **additional custom measurements** for different graphic placement goals. - Example idea shown: create another measurement and set it to lock to a different anatomical area such as **underarm**. This supports workflows where you switch between multiple measurement anchors for the same graphic.
